name: Implication chain with a conflict (DPLL)
note: DPLL: clauses 1–3 form a unit chain, a = T forces b = T forces c = T with no decision. g occurs only positively, so it is a pure literal (g = T). With no unit or pure literal left, DPLL decides d = T; that forces e = T by clause 4 and empties clause 5, so it backtracks to d = F, which forces f = T (clause 6) and e = T (clause 7). Result 1110111 after 2 decisions and 1 backtrack. Set the value order to F first and the conflict never happens (1 decision, 0 backtracks); switch the pure literal rule off and g is forced later by unit propagation (clause 8) once f = T, at the cost of one more forced assignment. Hill climbing from 0000000 stops at 0001000 (h 7 of 8) on this formula.
